title: client.subgraph(name, getSdk) gives typed, authenticated access to a project's own subgraphs
content:
## URL derivation and caching

A subgraph is served at `<graphql base>/<name>` — for a Switchboard on `http://localhost:4001/graphql`, the `renown-read-model` subgraph is at `http://localhost:4001/graphql/renown-read-model`. `client.subgraph(name, getSdk)` derives that URL from the client's own `url`, keeps **one transport per name**, and hands the SDK the same auth middleware every reactor call goes through.

```tsx
const client = useSwitchboardClient();
const sdk = client.subgraph("renown-read-model", getRenownReadModelSdk);
const { renownUsers } = await sdk.RenownUsers([UNKNOWN_ADDRESS]);
```

The registry caches the **transport** per name but reuses the **SDK** only when the same factory function is passed again. Two callers with two different generated SDKs each get their own, rather than the first caller's methods appearing under the second caller's type.

## What you get, and what you don't

`subgraph` gives transport, auth and typing — nothing more. Results are **not cached**, produce **no change events** and never reach `useDocument`. Cache them with whatever the app already uses for server state.

## Generating the SDK

Point `graphql-codegen` at the subgraph's endpoint with the plugins `typescript`, `typescript-operations` and `typescript-graphql-request`. That last plugin emits `getSdk(client, withWrapper?)`, which is exactly the factory signature `subgraph` expects:

```typescript
export type SubgraphSdkFactory<TSdk> = (
  client: GraphQLClient,
  withWrapper?: SdkFunctionWrapper,
) => TSdk;
```

Pass the generated function straight in. `SdkFunctionWrapper` is re-exported from `@powerhousedao/reactor-browser`, so a hand-written SDK can name the type without depending on `graphql-request`. An SDK the client builds is **always** called with the auth wrapper, so a hand-written one must apply it to every operation, exactly as generated code does.

For a one-off query not worth generating an SDK for, `client.request` runs against the Switchboard's own endpoint through the same transport and auth.

**Verification tip:** the root supergraph federates every subgraph, so a subgraph's field is usually reachable at the base URL too. To prove a request hit the subgraph's own endpoint, query `_service { sdl }` — the root has no `_service` field.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/04-Reference/08-ReactorBrowserClient/03-SubgraphsAndAttachments.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
